Q1: A block of mass (m) = 1 nanogram and length= width = height=1 nanometer slides down an inclined plane from rest. The plane is at a constant angle ($\theta$) of 30$^o$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction ($\mu_k$) between the mass and the plane is 0.5. The acceleration due to gravity at the location is 10 m/s$^2$. The block slides down a total distance of 5 meters before it touches the ground. What is the total time taken by the block to travel the 5 meters?
Q2: A simple pendulum has a solid sphere of mass (m) 2.5 nanograms with a diameter of 1 nanometer and a string of negligible mass. The distance between the point of support and the center of the spherical mass is L = 2 meters. The acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s$^2$ at the location. Find the time period of this pendulum for small displacements.
Q3: A solid sphere (a rigid body) of mass (m) 4 nanograms and a diameter of 8 nanometers is released with a initial velocity of 3.001 x10$^8$ m/s from the top of an inclined plane at a height of 6 X 10$^8$ meters on Earth. Calculate the velocity of the solid sphere at the bottom of the plane using conservation of energy. The acceleration due to gravity at the location is 10 m/s$^2$.
